1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at comfortable size with readable line spacing in the body text and info callouts.

2.why: No italics or all-caps prose appear, and every paragraph is one or two short sentences (only the code strings are uppercase monospace).

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred card that would likely reflow acceptably, but all screenshots are desktop-width and no mobile rendering is demonstrated.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Enter the six-digit verification code.' and 'Each code works once if you cannot use your authenticator.' are brief and plain.

5.why: No sample input is shown for any field; the closest hints are 'six-digit' and 'Type: Time-based, 6 digits', with no worked example of the expected format.

6.why: Every screen contains only short sentences and no long paragraph must be read before pressing the primary button.

7.why: The 32-character setup key and the eight recovery codes are displayed as static text with no copy button, download, or print option, so they must be transcribed by hand.

8.why: Step 3 mentions scanning, but step 4 offers only 'Enter this setup key manually in your authenticator app' — no QR code or equivalent is ever displayed.

9.why: Nothing in the screenshots indicates autocomplete/one-time-code support; the email, phone, password and code fields show no autofill affordances or hints.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading and one dominant blue primary button, but there is no step indicator (e.g. 'Step 2 of 5') to show where the user is in the flow.

11.why: Each screen requests a single main action (verify identity, confirm authenticator, save codes), with secondary options clearly de-emphasised as links or grey buttons.

12.why: Confirmations such as 'MFA is active — Your authenticator and recovery codes are ready.' and 'Recovery code confirmed — That recovery code has been used and cannot be used again.' state outcome and next action.

13.why: 'Show setup key', 'Generate new recovery codes', 'Use another email' and 'Back to MFA status' allow retry and re-request without penalty, though there is no hide/mask toggle for revealed secrets.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but generic — it names neither the problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry warnings, or session clocks appear on any screen, so nothing imposes a reading or entry time limit in the observed flow.
